rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those unable to maintain piety and excellence in their homeland should migrate where they can; prophets and righteous people set the precedent, and there is no excuse for neglect.
rows.anchor: فليهاجر إلى حيث يتمكن فيه من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse urges migration from a place where sins are openly practiced.
rows.anchor: حث على الهجرة من البلد الذي يظهر فيه المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report promises Paradise to one who leaves one land for another to protect religion; the author distinguishes religious flight from worldly motives, especially when the destination is more sinful.
rows.anchor: إن من فر بدينه من أرض إلى أرض وجبت له الجنة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Inwardly, God’s presence has no limit: visions and unveilings never mean the seeker has reached the highest aim, since nearness and arrival have no endpoint; Rumi likewise urges continuing beyond each threshold.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى حضرة جلاله أنه لا نهاية لها فلا يغتر طالب بما يفتح عليه من أبواب المشاهدات والمكاشفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The patient keep their religion and its limits through persecution and suffering, including the pain of leaving family and homeland; their reward corresponds to what they endured and is beyond counting.
rows.anchor: الذين صبروا على دينهم ، فلم يتركوه للأذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains divine full recompense with the lexicon’s sense of giving or taking something in full.
rows.anchor: توفية الشيء بذله وافيا كاملا واستيفاؤه تناوله وافيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says scales are set for prayer, charity, and pilgrimage, but not for the afflicted: their reward is poured out until the healthy wish they had been cut with shears for such merit.
rows.anchor: أنه تنصب الموازين يوم القيامة لأهل الصلاة والصدقة والحج

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyan relates that the Prophet first sought more than tenfold reward for his community, then more than the seven-hundredfold described in 2:261, until this verse came and he stopped asking.
rows.anchor: قال سفيان : لما نزل {من جآء بالحسنة فله عشر أمثالها}

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says prophets are tested most, followed by those most like them; the trial matches religious firmness and continues until the person walks free of sin.
rows.anchor: قال : "الأنبياء ثم الأمثل فالأمثل يبتلى الرجل على حسب دينه"

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A person unable to attain a divinely assigned rank through deeds may be tried in body, wealth, or child; patience through the trial brings that rank.
rows.anchor: إن العبد إذا سبقت له من الله منزلة لم يبلغها بعمله ابتلاه الله في جسده

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The greatest reward accompanies the greatest trial; God tests those He loves, and acceptance earns His pleasure while resentment earns His displeasure.
rows.anchor: وإن أعظم الجزاء مع عظم البلاء ، وإن الله عز وجل إذا أحب قوما ابتلاهم

rows.speaker: البقلي
rows.claim: Al-Baqli describes the people through four qualities: faith, God-consciousness, excellence, and patience.
rows.anchor: وصف الله القوم بأربع خصال : بالإيمان والتقوى والإحسان والصبر

rows.speaker: البقلي
rows.claim: Their faith is direct knowledge of God and His attributes through God, without inference from created events.
rows.anchor: فأما إيمانهم فهو المعرفة بذاته وصفاته من غير استدلال بالحدثان

rows.speaker: البقلي
rows.claim: Their piety strips the self of attachment to created existence until they stand without a veil from God.
rows.anchor: تقواهم فتجريدهم أنفسهم عن الكون حتى قاموا بلا احتجاب عنه

rows.speaker: البقلي
rows.claim: Their excellence is perceiving divine vision in hearts and spirits through the unveiling of divine beauty; their patience is steadfastness in states while concealing the complete unveiling.
rows.anchor: وأما إحسانهم فإدراكهم رؤيته تعالى بقلوبهم وأرواحهم بنعت كشف جماله

rows.speaker: البقلي
rows.claim: True patience does not claim permanence after attaining it. Inwardly, God’s spacious earth is the heart, expanded by the Real.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة الصبر أن لا يدعي الديمومة بعد الاتصاف بها

rows.speaker: البقلي
rows.claim: The gnostic receives a worldly reward of extraordinary inspirations and arrivals, and an afterlife reward of immersion in eternity, annihilation in the Essence, and abiding in the attributes.
rows.anchor: فإذا كان العارف بهذه الأوصاف ، فله أجران : أجر الدنيا

rows.speaker: الحارث المحاسبي
rows.claim: Al-Harith al-Muhasibi defines patience as exposing oneself to the arrows of affliction.
rows.anchor: قال الحارث المحاسبي : الصبر التهدف لسهام البلاء

rows.speaker: طاهر المقدسي
rows.claim: Tahir al-Maqdisi distinguishes patience from, for, upon, and within God; the least difficult is patience in obeying God, for which this verse promises reward.
rows.anchor: وقال طاهر المقدسي : الصبر على وجوه صبر منه وصبر له وصبر عليه

rows.speaker: يوسف بن الحسين
rows.claim: Yusuf ibn al-Husayn says the patient person does not merely endure calamity while showing aversion, but delights in patience until reaching contentment.
rows.anchor: وقال يوسف بن الحسين : ليس بصابر من يتجرع المصيبة ويبدي فيها الكراهة

rows.speaker: ابن الفارض
rows.claim: Ibn al-Farid’s cited verse says one who wastes life has no share of its wine-like blessing.
rows.anchor: على نفسه قليبك من ضاع عمره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some attain a share of this love but not fully; others never reach spiritual satiation, which is the state of perfection.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من له نصيب من هذا الأمر لكن لا على وجه الكمال

rows.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ الرازي
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Muadh wrote that love’s cup had intoxicated him; Abu Yazid replied that the strong keep drinking without exhausting the drink or becoming satiated, even after seven seas.
rows.anchor: حكي أن يحيى بن معاذ الرازي رضي الله عنه : كتب إلى أبي يزيد البسطامي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse encourages the Prophet to endure unbelievers’ harm and answer their wrongdoing with goodness; patient restraint merits esteem here and reward in the afterlife, unlike their evil conduct.
rows.anchor: بيان لمحاسن الأعمال الجارية بين العبد وبين الرب ترغيبا لرسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the reading of good and evil as individual kinds, both vary internally—good deeds from removing harm upward, and sins from minor to major—so the second negating particle is not merely emphatic, as al-Kashshaf indicates.
rows.anchor: إذا فسرت الحسنة والسيئة بالجنس على أن يكون المعنى لا تستوي الحسنات إذ هي متفاوتة في أنفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repel an enemy’s evil by the best available good, such as kindness to an offender; this exceeds simple forgiveness, and the command’s wording intensifies the call to answer with goodness.
rows.anchor: ادفع السيئة حين اعترضتك من بعض أعاديك بالتي هي أحسن ما يمكن دفعها به من الحسنات كالإحسان إلى من أساء

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet practiced what he taught: keep ties with one who cuts them, pardon the wrongdoer, and treat an offender well.
rows.anchor: صل من قطعك واعف عمن ظلمك وأحسن إلى من أساء إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase answers the question of how to repel evil; using the superlative ‘best’ makes the instruction stronger, since one who repels with the best can easily use a lesser good.
rows.anchor: وضع أحسن موضع الحسنة ؛ لأنه أبلغ في الدفع بالحسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The result is that a hostile opponent becomes like a compassionate close friend.
rows.anchor: فإذا فعلت ذلك صار عدوك المشاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report identifies Abu Sufyan ibn Harb as the occasion of revelation: after severe enmity, a marriage tie softened him toward Muslims, and his conversion made him a close ally through Islam and kinship.
rows.anchor: روي : أنها نزلت في أبي سفيان بن حرب ، وذلك أنه لان للمسلمين بعد الشدة

rows.speaker: الإمام الأعظم
rows.claim: A Persian anecdote attributed to the Greatest Imam says that when someone spoke ill of him, he praised that person until the other began speaking well of him.
rows.anchor: از امام اعظم نقلست كسى بمن رسانندكه مرابدمى كويد من درشان او سحن نيكو ترمى كويم

rows.speaker: البقلي
rows.claim: Al-Baqli says good character differs from bad character; one should replace blameworthy traits with praiseworthy ones, especially forbearance, which turns enemies into friends and repays anger, oppression, and bad treatment with patience, pardon, and generosity.
rows.anchor: قال البقلي : بين الله ها هنا أن الخلق الحسن ليس كالخلق السيىء

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata distinguishes those who enter and leave divine service with proper conduct from those who behave badly in service; poor manners in nearness are graver than at a distance.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : لا يستوي من أحسن الدخول في خدمتنا

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: God may pardon ignorant people for major sins yet hold the elect accountable for even a glance or turning aside.
rows.anchor: فقد يصفح عن الجهال في الكبائر ويؤاخذ الصديقون باللحظة والالتفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word talqiya can mean bringing something before someone; here it means being given the virtue of answering wrong with good, a quality that restrains revenge.
rows.anchor: التلقية : (جيزى بيش كسى آوردن)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only those characterized by patience receive this virtue, because patience holds the self back from retaliation.
rows.anchor: فإنها تحبس النفس عن الانتقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person of great allotted share has noble psychic qualities and spiritual strength; revenge reflects a weak self affected by external events, while inner strength makes bearing them easy.
rows.anchor: من الفضائل النفسانية والقوة الروحانية ، فإن الاشتغال بالانتقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purifying the self makes sweetness and bitterness equal, so an unwelcome event feels as though absent; the verse praises patience and an allotted share.
rows.anchor: والحاصل : أنه يلزم تزكية النفس حتى يستوي الحلو والمر

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Junayd says only a person favored by God’s special care is granted this station.
rows.anchor: قال الجنيد قدس سره في قوله : وما يلقاها إلا ذو حظ عظيم

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata interprets the person of great share as one who knows God and His days.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : ذو معرفة بالله وأيامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the construction ‘if Satan should incite you,’ in is conditional and ma reinforces the condition, which licenses the emphatic nūn on its verb.
rows.anchor: إن شرطية ، وما مزيدة لتأكيد معنى الشرط والاستلزام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nazgh literally resembles a prick or prod; it describes Satanic whispering because it urges evil and stirs a person toward what is improper.
rows.anchor: والنزغ شبه النخس كما في "الإرشاد"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He offers two grammatical readings of ‘from Satan’: an originating source, or a descriptive source noun that abstracts another instigator from Satan and calls it a nazigh.
rows.anchor: فمن ابتدائية ؛ أي : نزغ صادر من جهته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning means Satan may whisper and divert the Prophet from the commanded best response, calling him toward its opposite.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : وأن يوسوس إليك الشيطان ويصرفك عما وصيت به

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Inwardly, the seeker faces many spiritual highway robbers: ego, desire, worldly ornament, pleasure, and status can divert a person from the quest, destroy the goal, and leave the person deprived of it.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن في قطاع الطريق على أرباب الطلب لكثرة فمن يصرفه عن طلبه قاطع من القطاع من النفس والهوى والدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author invokes the plea for refuge from falling away after spiritual ascent and a divine herald’s lament over how many companions have been left behind.
rows.anchor: كما قيل نعوذ بالله من الحور بعد الكور وينادي عليه منادي العزة وكم مثلها فارقتها وهي تصفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qatl is a curse or prayer for destruction, as in ‘cursed be man’; it later functions as condemnation, and khars means conjecture without reliable knowledge.
rows.anchor: دعاء عليهم كقوله قتل الإنسان ما أكفره وأصله الدعاء بالقتل والهلاك

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib explains ghamr as water that covers its bed; by analogy ignorance overwhelms and covers the person, and the word also describes severe afflictions.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب أصل الغمر إزالة أثر الشيء ومنه قيل للماء الكثير الذي يزيد أثر مسيله غمر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the conjecturers as soothsayers.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهدهم الكهنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A conjecturer is a liar even when his guess happens to be true, since it was made without knowledge, reliable probability, or report; these conjecturers are liars who assert what has no basis.
rows.anchor: كل قول مقول عن ظن وتخمين يقال له خرص سواء كان ذلك مطابقا للشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘In a ghamra’ means engulfed in ignorance and misguidance that conceals the afterlife; ‘sahun’ adds that they neglect what they were commanded.
rows.anchor: غمرة} من الجهل والضلال تغمرهم وتغشاهم عن أمر الآخرة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says sahw is error from inadvertence: what was not produced by one’s actions is excused, whereas conduct generated by one’s own act is accountable and is the condemned kind here.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : السهو خطأ عن غفلة وذلك ضربان أحدهما أن لا يكون

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Kashf al-Asrar identifies the conjecturers as those who divided Mecca’s mountain passes and coordinated claims about the Prophet to turn visitors away from Islam and his company.
rows.anchor: وفي كشف الأسرار الخراصون هم المقتسمون الذين اقتسموا عقاب مكة واقتسموا القول في النبي

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Inwardly, do not treat ego, desire, this world, or the next as rival objects of devotion beside God; monotheism means severing attachment and fleeing to God, whose true fugitive finds rest with Him.
rows.anchor: ولا تجعلوا مع الله في المعرفة بوحدانيته إلها آخر من النفوس والهوى والدنيا والآخرة فتعبدونها بالميل إليها

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The warning is against the painful distance and duality of associating anything with God in existence, for the text says He does not forgive association.
rows.anchor: أخوفكم أليم عقوبة البعد وعذاب الاثنينية إذا أشركتم به في الوجود فإنه لا يغفر أن يشرك به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Likewise’ compares the denial of Quraysh and Arab idolaters with earlier peoples, who called every messenger a sorcerer or madman; miracles were dismissed as magic and resurrection as madness, so the Prophet should not grieve.
rows.anchor: أي الأمر وهو أمر الأمم السالفة بالنسبة إلى رسلهم من ما ذكر من تكذيب قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question asks whether earlier generations advised later ones to use the same slur, marveling that the accusation recurred across eras.
rows.anchor: إنكار وتعجيب من حالهم وإجماعهم على تفرق أزمانهم على تلك الكلمة الشنيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects mutual advice as the explanation because the generations were separated; their shared insult instead arose from each group’s innate transgression and wicked disposition.
rows.anchor: إضراب عن كون مدار اتفاقهم على الشر تواصيهم بذلك لبعد الزمان وعدم تلاقيهم

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Inwardly, rebellious souls in every age share a satanic nature of refusal, pride, and defiance, so they reject outward prophets and inward divine inspirations alike as magic or madness; abundance, comfort, arrogance, and wealth feed their transgression.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن أرباب النفوس المتمردة من الأولين والآخرين مركوزة في جبلتهم طبيعة الشيطنة من التمرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two upper bodies and two lower plant forms supply food—grains, fruit, and fodder; the unlinked opening clauses imitate enumeration and rebuke failure to give thanks, while the star clause is joined because upper and lower pairs contrast and all obey God.
rows.anchor: وكلاهما من قبيل النبات الذي هو أصل الرزق من الحبوب والثمار والحشيش للدواب وإخلاء الجمل الأولى عن العطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominal syntax for these four forms, unlike the human addressee, marks their difference in essence and attributes.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت هذه الأربعة مغايرة لجنس الإنسان في ذاته وصفاته غير النظم بإيرادها في صورة الاسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, the star is the intellect that guides toward knowledge but fades before divine realities unless it receives divine unveiling; the tree is thought, confined to natural, imaginative, and bodily powers and unable to grasp realities fully.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى سجود نجم العقل الذي به يهتدي إلى معرفة الأشياء واستهلاكه وتلاشيه عند النظر إلى الحقائق الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reason and thought circle the created cosmos but melt when they look to the Creator; being created and bounded, they cannot comprehend the eternal God, whom people have not measured as He deserves.
rows.anchor: العقل والفكر جالا حول سرادق الكون فإذا نظرا إلى المكون ذابا وكيف لا وهما مخلوقان محصوران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘He raised the heaven’ means God created it visibly elevated in place and rank, as the source of His judgments and commands and the abode of angels.
rows.anchor: خلقها مرفوعة محلا كما هو محسوس مشاهد وكذا رتبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others explain the raising as lifting heaven above earth to serve as a roof for creatures, with five hundred years’ distance between them; heaven was smoke evaporated above the earth’s water.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : رفعها من السفل إلى العلو سقفا لمصالح العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘He set the balance’ means instituting justice: giving each deserving person their due and each rights-holder their right so the world remains ordered; a Prophetic saying links the order of heaven and earth to justice.
rows.anchor: أي شرع العدل وأمر به بأن وفر كل مستحق لما استحقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations identify the balance as the Quran or as instruments such as scales and measures by which people know quantities and fulfill just dealings; Sa‘di al-Mufti and al-Zamakhshari favor the concrete measuring sense in context.
rows.anchor: قيل فعلى هذا الميزان هو القرآن وقيل هو ما يعرف به مقادير الأشياء من ميزان وميكال ونحوهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing weight with justice means making it straight; ‘weight’ is knowing a thing’s measure and extends to fairness in all intended acts and words.
rows.anchor: قوموا وزنكم بالعدل أي اجعلوه مستقيما به وفي المفردات الوزن معرفة قدر الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not diminish the balance or what it measures: it should be even, the purpose for which it was established; the lexicons distinguish shortchanging from the verb for commercial loss.
rows.anchor: يقال : خسرت الشيء بالفتح واحسرته نقصته وبابه ضرب

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Sa‘di al-Mufti says the command concerns not reducing the weighed goods, not damaging the scale; the passage first requires fairness, then prohibits excess, then shortchanging, and repeats ‘balance’ for emphasis.
rows.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي : المراد لا تنقصوا الموزون في الميزان لا الميزان نفسه

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says the repeated emphasis warns scale users to avoid shame when the Judgment balance is set; his Persian verses say every small or large shortfall and hidden fraud will be exposed.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : أين همه تأكيد اهل ترازو راجهت آنست كه بوقت وضع ميزان

rows.speaker: مالك بن دينار
rows.claim: Malik ibn Dinar visited a dying neighbor who described two mountains of fire; the family said he used one measure when giving and another when receiving, and destroying them did not lessen his ordeal.
rows.anchor: روي عن مالك بن دينار رحمه الله أنه دخل على جار له احتضر فقال

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib gives two compatible readings: pursue fairness and avoid injustice in weighing, or ensure one’s deeds do not leave the Resurrection balance deficient; Quranic loss concerns the latter, not worldly trade losses.
rows.anchor: وفي المفردات قوله : ولا تخسروا الميزان يجوز أن يكون إشارة إلى تحري العدالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Haqqa is a name for the Resurrection: from haqq, ‘to be due and established,’ since its coming is obligatory and certain; al-Raghib instead says recompense becomes due then, a figurative attribution. He cites 20:15.
rows.anchor: هي منأسماء القيامة من حق يحق بالكسر إذا وجب وثبت لأنها يحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘What is the Haqqa?’ originally asks what it is like in state and character; putting the explicit noun where a pronoun could stand underscores its majesty and terror.
rows.anchor: الأصل ما هي أي أي شيء هي في حالها وصفتها فإن ما قد يطلب بها الصفة والحال فوضع الظاهر موضع المضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes parse the repeated question as nested nominal clauses, with the repeated noun linking them; the author’s preferred analysis makes interrogative ‘what’ the predicate, highlighting that the Haqqa is a wondrous, terrifying event.
rows.anchor: ومقتضى التحقيق أن تكون ما الاستفهامية خبرا لما بعدها فإن مناط الفائدة بيان أن الحاقة أمر بديع وخطب فظيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘What could make you know’ derives from knowledge and means ‘what informed you, Muhammad’; the question is parsed as a subject and predicate, with the following question as its second object.
rows.anchor: من الدراة بمعنى العلم يقال دراه ودرى به أي علم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated question magnifies the Hour’s horror beyond the knowledge or imagination of creatures; whatever state one imagines is still less than it. One view says the Prophet knew it would occur but not its full manner; it may address hearers through him.
rows.anchor: بحيث لا يكاد تبلغه دراية أحد ولا وهمه وكيفما قدرت حالها فهي أعظم من ذلك وأعظم

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Inwardly, the Haqqa is the absolute singular manifestation within unity that annihilates all distinctions under the sovereignty of the One, the Subduer; it is called true because it is established in itself.
rows.anchor: يشير بالحاقة إلى التجلي الإحدى الإطلاقي في مراءة الواحدية المفني للكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamud are Salih’s people, their name linked to a small water source without replenishment; ‘Ad are Hud’s people and also a tribe name treated as feminine.
rows.anchor: من الثمد وهو الماء القليل الذي لا مادة له

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Inwardly, the human has an unseen conceptual form and a visible concrete form, both eternally known to God; His prior knowledge encompasses all things, which manifest His names and attributes.
rows.anchor: للإنسان صورة علمية غيبية وصورة عينية شهادية وهو من حيث كلتا الصورتين مذكور عند الله أزلا وأبدا

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The question whether a time passed when the human was forgotten is answered negatively: all are present to God’s knowledge, including the human created in His image; only the veiled fail to recognize this.
rows.anchor: وهل للاستفهام الإنكاري بخلاف المحجوبين عن علم المعرفة والحكمة الإلهية

rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: Ja‘far al-Sadiq glosses the question as asking whether there was ever a time when God was not remembering the human.
rows.anchor: هل أتى عليك يا إنسان وقت لم يكن الله ذاكرا لك فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘We created the human’ means the body; explicit naming reinforces the statement. The nutfa develops into a clot at forty days, a morsel at eighty, and receives the spirit at one hundred twenty.
rows.anchor: أي خلقناه يعني جسمه والإظهار لزيادة التقرير

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from al-Dahhak through Ibn Abbas says Adam’s creation proceeded through forty years each in clay, dark mud, and baked clay before the spirit was breathed into him; what took Adam years took descendants days.
rows.anchor: سنين في آدم كان أياما في أولاده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take the first human as Adam and the second as his descendants, with ‘time’ an unknown long duration; the author prefers ‘human’ to mean the species in both places, recalling its origin from nothing and humble fluid to rebut denial of resurrection.
rows.anchor: وحمل بعضهم الإنسان الأول على آدم والثاني على أولاده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amshaj means mixed elements; it is a plural-form adjective for the single nutfa because the intended matter combines male and female fluids, whose colors, consistencies, and properties differ.
rows.anchor: جمع مشج كسبب أو كتف على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the male fluid is white and thick and the female fluid yellow and thin; the child resembles whichever prevails, with nerves, bones, and strength from the male and flesh, blood, and hair from the female, according to a Prophetic report.
rows.anchor: ماء الرجل أبيض غليظ فيه قوة العقد

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report says each newborn has some of the soil of its burial place mixed into its nutfa.
rows.anchor: ما من مولدو إلا وقد ذر على نطفته من تربة حفرته

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the mixed nutfa includes menstrual blood, which stops when pregnancy begins; al-Qamus likewise defines it as mixed with the woman’s fluid and blood.
rows.anchor: نطفة مشيجة بدم وهو دم الحيض فإذا حبلت ارتفع الحيض

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib interprets the mixture as the different powers God placed in the nutfa, pointing to the successive stages of creation in 23:12–14.
rows.anchor: هو عبارة عما جعل الله بالنطفة من القوى المختلفة المشار إليها بقوله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says amshaj means colors and stages.
rows.anchor: فيكون معنى أمشاج ألوان وأطوار على ما قال قتادة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Inwardly, the mixed nutfa is the interweaving of receptive potential and active power, represented by the most holy and holy effusions, respectively likened to male and female fluids.
rows.anchor: أي من نطفة قوة القابلية الممتشجة المختلطة بنطفة قوة الفاعلية أي خلقناه من نطفة الفيض الأقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Testing him’ is a prospective state: God intends to test through future obligations, making people’s acceptance, rejection, felicity, and misery manifest in detail after being known generally.
rows.anchor: حال مقدرة من فاعل خلقنا أي مريدين ابتلاءه واختباره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing and sight equip a person to hear revealed signs and witness created signs, enabling the intended test; intellect is omitted because the passage names its instruments and usual route to completion.
rows.anchor: ليتمكن من استماع الآيات التنزيلية ومشاهدة الآيات التكوينية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intensive forms signal the completeness of God’s favor; ‘seeing’ is the second object after the first object of ‘made.’
rows.anchor: وفي اختيار صيغة المبالغة إشارة إلى كمال إحسنه إليه وتمام إنعامه

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Inwardly, God becomes the servant’s hearing and sight: by Him the servant hears and sees every audible and visible thing, with nothing escaping perception.
rows.anchor: كما قال كنت سمعه وبصره فبي يسمع وبي يبصر فلا يفوته شيء من المسموعات

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان المغربي
rows.claim: Abu Uthman al-Maghribi describes nine inner mixtures: hearing, sight, and tongue tempt; ego, desire, and Satan oppose faith; intellect, spirit, and heart believe.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عثمان المغربي قدس سره ابتلى الله الخلق بتسعة أمشاج

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان المغربي
rows.claim: With divine aid, intellect masters the heart, captures ego and desire, and makes the self kin to spirit and desire kin to intellect, so God’s word prevails; he cites the command to fight until there is no fitna.
rows.anchor: فإذا أيد الله العبد بالمعونة قهر العقل على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance follows the gift of senses and explains it: God showed the ways of good and evil, salvation and ruin, through revealed signs and proofs; it means direction, not guidance that necessarily brings attainment, as in 90:10.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أريناه وعرفناه طريق الخير والشر والنجاة والهلاك بإنزال الآيات ونصب الدلائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Irshad reads ‘whether grateful or ungrateful’ as two enabled states: the thankful person affirms divine benefaction and unity, while the ungrateful person denies it; gratitude acknowledges the benefactor and disbelief begins with denial.
rows.anchor: فالشاكر الموحد والكفور الجاحد لأن الشكر الإقرار بالنمعم ورأس الكفر إن جحوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wayl means severe evil, ruin, or painful punishment; Ibn Kaysan calls it the utterance of a distressed person in affliction, implying that the addressee deserves calamity, while another derivation links it to sorrow.
rows.anchor: شدة الشر أو الهلاك أو العذاب الأليم ، وقال ابن كيسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wayl can begin a sentence despite being indefinite because it functions as a curse or prayer for harm, as discussed earlier in al-Mursalat.
rows.anchor: وهو مبتدأ وإن كان نكرة لوقوعه في موقع الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutaffifin are those who deprive people of their rights in measuring and weighing; tatfif is secretly cheating by giving a buyer less than the full due, often in a slight amount that escapes notice.
rows.anchor: فإن التطفيف البخس في الكيل والوزن والنقص والخيانة فيهما بأن لا يعطي المشتري حقه تاما كاملا

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines short-measuring as reducing the buyer’s share when fulfilling a measure; Sa‘di al-Mufti says the intensive pattern suits their habitual cheating, though it could be causative.
rows.anchor: يقال طفف الكيل قلل نصيب المكيل له في إيفائه واستيفائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet arrived in Medina when its people were among the worst measurers, recited the newly revealed surah, and five public wrongs brought five calamities; after they complied, they became the fairest measurers.
rows.anchor: روى أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قدم المدينة وكان أهلها من أبخس الناس كيلا

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali saw a man weighing saffron and adding extra; he told him first to establish the proper measure, then to give extra as he wished, distinguishing obligation from charity.
rows.anchor: إنه مر برجل يزن الزعفران وقد أرجح فقال أقم الوزن بالقسط

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas warns non-Arabs that measure and scale were the two practices by which earlier peoples perished, singling them out because they used both methods together.
rows.anchor: إنكم معشر الأعاجم وليتم أمرين بهما هلك من كان قبلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause explains how the cheaters shortchange others and why they merit condemnation: when receiving measured goods in a purchase, they take the full amount and more.
rows.anchor: صفة كاشفة للمطففين شارحة لكيفية تطفيفهم الذي استحقوا به الذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iktiāl means taking goods by measure, like ittizān means taking by weight; ‘upon the people’ can imply dominance or seizure, not merely receiving one’s due.
rows.anchor: أي من الناس مكيلهم بحكم الشراء ونحوه والاكتيال الأخذ بالكيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their istīfā’ is not fair receipt of an exact right but taking an abundant amount through any available trick, including packing measures, shaking them, and stealing from their rims and scale tongues.
rows.anchor: بل مجرد الأخذ الوافي الوافر حسبما أرادوا بأي وجه يتيسر من وجوه الحيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When they measure or weigh goods for others, the original preposition meaning ‘for’ is omitted and the verb takes the object directly.
rows.anchor: أي وإذا كالوا للناس أو وزنوا لهم المبيع ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attached pronoun is accusative as the object, not nominative emphasis on the plural verb; Quranic spelling and comparison with other plural forms support that parsing.
rows.anchor: فلفظ هم منصوب المحل على المفعولية لا مرفوعة على التأكيد للواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yukhsirun means they reduce others’ rights, contrary to the purpose of measures and scales, which is equality and justice.
rows.anchor: أي ينقصون حقوقهم مع إن وضع الكيل والوزن إنما هو للتسوية والتعديل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, the limited self shortchanges the spirit in true, essential monotheism because it lacks capacity; that tawhid has no counterpart and should not be weighed, while formal monotheism is the self’s due from the spirit.
rows.anchor: فيه إشارة إلى حال النفس القاصرة في التوحيد الحققي فإنها إذا أعطته الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Do they not think?’ is an interrogative hamza with negation, not an alerting particle, since removing the latter would leave the meaning intact; it may also urge them to think.
rows.anchor: بل الهمزة الاستفهامية الإنكارية داخلة على لا النافية وجوز أن تكون للعرض والتحضيض على الظن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day is immense and people will be reckoned for even a speck or mustard seed; mention of mere supposition intensifies the warning, since even weak belief would deter cheating, while believers need certainty.
rows.anchor: ومحاسبون فيه على مقدار الذرة والخردلة فإن من يظن ذلك وإن كان ظنا ضعيفا في حد الشك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘The day people stand’ is governed by an implied ‘I mean’; standing ‘for the Lord of the worlds’ can mean at His command, for His accounting, or from graves as He returns souls to bodies.
rows.anchor: منصوب بإضمار أعنى {لرب العالمين} بتقدير المضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says people stand before God for forty years; another gives three years, with sweat reaching their ears and no news or order coming to them.
rows.anchor: روى إنهم يقومون بين يدي الله تعالى أربعين عاما وفي رواية ثلاثة سنة من سني الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian verse says the awe of that station leaves no one able to speak.
rows.anchor: وآن مقام هيبت باشدكه كس رازهره سخن نباشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For believers, the waiting is as brief as the time it takes to leave a prescribed prayer.
rows.anchor: وأما في حق المؤمن فيكون المكت كقدر إنصرافهم من صلاة مكتوبة

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qashani interprets what unbelievers store as corrupt beliefs and vicious dispositions kept in their inner selves.
rows.anchor: بما يوعونه في وعاء أنفسهم وبواطنهم من الاعتقادات الفاسدة

rows.speaker: نجم الدين
rows.claim: Najm al-Din describes them as drowning in worldly desires and burning in the fire of punishment to come.
rows.anchor: وقال نجمد الدين من إغراقهم في بحر الشهوات الدنيوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to announce painful punishment addresses the unbelievers; the punishment is maximally painful, and announcing it ironically mocks them because good news ordinarily means welcome tidings.
rows.anchor: مؤلم غاية الإيلام لأن علمه تعالى بذلك على الوجه المذكور

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says the threat also hints at believers’ bodily and spiritual comfort in reward; ‘except those who believe’ is a disconnected exception, placing believers outside the unbelievers addressed.
rows.anchor: يعني خبركن ايشانرا بعذاب دردناك وفيه رمز إلى تبشير المؤمنين بالثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faithful have sincere belief, including knowledge that cleanses hearts of the self’s traits, and righteous deeds that include commanded worship and acquisition of virtues.
rows.anchor: إيمانا صادقا وأيضا الإيمان العلمي بتصفية قلوبهم عن كدر صفات النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reward is unbroken and enduring; ‘not bestowed as a favor’ is another possible meaning, though uninterrupted reward is more apparent, since even the capacity and guidance to act are God’s favor.
rows.anchor: أي غير مقطوع بل متصل دائم من منه منا بمعنى قطعه قطعا

rows.speaker: حسن البصري
rows.claim: Hasan al-Basri recalls people who gave away worldly wealth generously without reminding recipients of their favor.
rows.anchor: حسن بصري قدس سره : كفت كساني را يافتم كه ايشان بدنيا جوانمرد وسخى بودند

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qashani reads the reward as enduring traces and attributes in the garden of soul and heart, free from corruption and materiality.
rows.anchor: لهم أجر من ثواب الآثار والصفات فيج نة النفس والقلب غير مقطوع

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Inwardly, those believing from spirit, secret, heart, and spiritual powers, and doing good by turning from the world toward God, receive reward through God’s grace and mercy rather than self-effort or self-congratulation.
rows.anchor: إلا الذين آمنوا من الروح والسر والقلب وقواهم الروحانية وعملوا الصالحات من الأعراض عن الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kanud is the oath’s answer and means rejecting a blessing or being intensely ungrateful; Kinda’s name is linked to an ancestor who rejected favor and left his people.
rows.anchor: جواب القسم يقال كند النعمة كنودا كفر بها فالكنود بالضم كفران النعمة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi gives regional meanings for kanud: disobedient in Kinda, stingy among Banu Malik, and ungrateful among Mudar and Rabi‘a.
rows.anchor: الكنود بلسان كندة العاصي وبلسان بني مالك البخيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Human’ refers to some or to the human kind, and the lām in ‘to his Lord’ gives emphasis or restriction while also fitting the rhyme.
rows.anchor: فقوله لربه متعلق بكنود قدم عليه لإفادة التخصيص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the surah came after a month without news of an expedition to Banu Kinana; hypocrites claimed its members were killed, so the surah informed the Prophet of their safety and raid and reproached the rumor-mongers.
rows.anchor: روى أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعث إلى ناس من بني كنانة سرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath’s ‘charging horses’ can mean the known horses of that expedition or all horses charging in God’s cause; either way their noble qualities warrant the oath, and the fighters’ merit is greater still.
rows.anchor: فاللام في العاديات إن كانت للعهد كان المقسم به خيل تلك السرية وإن كانت للجنس كان ذلك قسما بكل خيل عدت

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet defines the ungrateful person as one who beats his servant, eats alone, and withholds his gift.
rows.anchor: وعنه عليه السلام الكنود هو الذي يضرب عبده ويأكل وحده ويمنع رفده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hatim al-Ta’i exemplifies generosity, Abu Habahib extreme stinginess, and Ash‘ab extreme greed, illustrated by comic tales of expecting food or gifts wherever he went.
rows.anchor: يقال كان ثلاثة نفر من العرب في عصر وحد أحدهم آية في السخاء وهو خاتم الطائي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the ungrateful person complains repeatedly about misfortunes while forgetting blessings.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن لكنود أي لوام لبه يذكر المصيبات وينسى النعم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda compares kanud to barren land that yields nothing, as though the word were a reversal of nakd.
rows.anchor: قليل الخير من الأرض الكنود التي لا تنبت شيئا كأنه مقلوب النكد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The loss is grave because the servant sins against the Lord and against immense benefaction; the indefinite form may also mark a distinctive kind of loss beyond ordinary human usage.
rows.anchor: والذنب يعظم إما لعظم من في حقه الذنب أو لأنه في مقابلة النعمة العظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those exempted have certain knowledge that only God truly acts, break through the veil of time, acquire enduring virtues, and profit by exchanging transient goods for lasting ones; this perfects the self.
rows.anchor: بالله الإيمان العلمي اليقيني وعرفوا أن لا مؤثر بالحقيقة إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some groups infer from the exception that grave sinners remain forever in loss; the author replies that the unexcepted may be eternally punished if unbelieving, enter the Fire if unpardoned sinners, or lose high degrees if forgiven.
rows.anchor: واستدل بعض الطوائف بالآية على أن مرتكب الكبيرة مخلد لأنه لم يستثن من الخسران إلا الذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutual exhortation to truth perfects others: it means affirming enduring, undeniable truth, including faith in God and following His books and messengers in belief and action.
rows.anchor: بيان لتكميلهم لغيرهم أي وصى بعضهم بعضا بالأمر الثابت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exhorting one another to patience means resisting desired sins, performing difficult obedience, and receiving trials from God with inward and outward contentment; it is emphasized either for its importance or to distinguish worship from servitude.
rows.anchor: أي عن المعاصي التي تشتاق إليها النفس بحكم الجبلة البشرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God names the path to profit rather than enumerating loss, both to focus on eternal success and to leave other losses unstated as an act of generosity.
rows.anchor: ولعله سبحانه إنما ذكر سبب الربح دون الخسران اكتفاء ببيان المقصود

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report swears that Abu Jahl is in loss except for four qualities, represented respectively by Abu Bakr’s faith, Umar’s good works, Uthman’s truth, and Ali’s patience; Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas gave this gloss from the pulpit.
rows.anchor: وروى عنه عليه السلام أنه قال أقسم ربكم بآخر النهار أن أبا جهل لفي خسر إلا الذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi‘i says that if this surah alone had been revealed to people, it would have sufficed them; another report says it encompasses all Quranic learning.
rows.anchor: أنها سورة لو لم ينزل إلى الناس إلا هي لكفتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wayl means woe or ruin; an indefinite noun can begin the sentence because it functions as a curse invoking destruction or severe harm.
rows.anchor: وهو مبتدأ وساغ الابتداء به مع كونه نكرة لأنه دعاء عليهم بالهلكة أو بشدة الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamz and lamz literally suggest breaking and stabbing, then refer to faulting people through contemptuous gestures or verbal attacks; lexicographers differ over whether the two terms target face or back.
rows.anchor: الهمز الكسر واللمز الطعن شاعا في الكسر من إعراض الناس والطعن فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pattern can indicate habitual action; Ibn Qutayba distinguishes forms for one who is mocked and one who mocks others.
rows.anchor: وبناء فعلة يدل على الاعتياد فلا قال ضحكة ولعنة إلا للمكثير المتعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was said to concern al-Akhnas ibn Shariq or al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, each of whom backbit the Messenger; the author prefers general application because it says ‘every.’
rows.anchor: ونزلوها في الأخنس بن شريف أو في الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A hadith contrasts the believer, who is discerning, cautious, deliberate, learned, and pious, with the hypocrite, who habitually slanders and behaves like a heedless firewood collector.
rows.anchor: المؤمن كيس فطن حذر وقاف متثبت لا يعجل عالم ورع

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qashani says fault-finding combines ignorance, anger, and animality: the fault-finder seeks superiority by harming others and projecting faults, unaware that this is itself a vice and that merely lacking a vice is no virtue.
rows.anchor: الهمز واللمز رذيلتان مركبتان من الجهل والغضب والكلب لأنهما يتضمنان الأذية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accumulating wealth explains the mockery: self-admiration over money makes a person imagine wealth confers honor and superiority, so he belittles others; the phrase is appositional rather than a grammatical adjective of the indefinite ‘every.’
rows.anchor: بدل من كل كأنه قيل ويل للذي جمع مالا وإنما وصفه الله بهذا الوصف المعنوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He repeatedly counts and hoards wealth without discharging God’s due; an alternate reading with the doubled consonant separated supports the sense ‘counted it,’ while another reading makes it provisions for future calamities.
rows.anchor: أي عده مرة بعد أخرى من غير أن يؤدي حق الله منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accumulation signals appetitive power and repeated counting signals ignorance: wealth itself attracts the calamities through which divine wisdom disperses it, so it cannot ward them off.
rows.anchor: لا يعلم أن نفس ذلك المال هو الذي يجر إليه النوائب

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Inwardly, the collected wealth is a hoard of blameworthy morals and low qualities, treated as provision for the stages of the afterlife and entry into God’s presence.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية جمع مال الأخلاق الذميمة والأوصاف الرديئة وجعله عدة منازل الآخرة والدخول على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person behaves as though wealth will immortalize him, building sturdy structures, planting trees, and digging rivers; the belief is figurative, not an actual conviction.
rows.anchor: أي يعمل من تشييد البنيان وإيثاقه بالصخر والآجر وغرس الأشجار

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Tahir says the miser thinks his money will convey him to an immortal station; the past tense depicts wealth as having already guaranteed survival and safety from death.
rows.anchor: يظن أنه ماله يوصله إلى مقام الخلد وإنما قال أخلده

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan observes that death is certain, yet resembles a matter doubted by people who lack certainty.
rows.anchor: ما رأيت يقينا لا شك فيه أشبه بشك لا يقين فيه كالموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rebukes the false belief that wealth makes a person immortal; it may also rebuke the earlier mockery and answer an implied oath that the person will certainly be cast down.
rows.anchor: ردع له عن ذلك الحسبان الباطل يعني نه نانست كه آدمى ندارد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another grammatical reading refers the dual verb to both the hamza and the lamza, supported by a recitation that uses the dual form.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم ولك أن ترد الضمير إلى كل من الهمزة واللمزة ويؤيده قراءة لينبذان على التثنية
